title: Matrix
description:
Write a class `Matrix` of `double`s with a size chosen at run time.

- `Matrix(std::size_t rows, std::size_t columns)`: every element starts at 0. Store the numbers in **one** `std::vector<double>`; the element at (row, column) lives at index `row * columns + column`.
- `rows()` and `columns()`.
- `operator()(row, column)` in const and non-const versions, so `m(1, 2) = 5.0;` and `double x{ m(1, 2) };` both work.
- `operator==`.
- `operator+` (same-sized matrices) and `operator*` (matrix multiplication: the result has the rows of the left and the columns of the right; element (r, c) is the sum over k of `left(r, k) * right(k, c)`).
- `static Matrix identity(std::size_t n)`: n × n with 1 on the diagonal.

The tests only add and multiply matrices whose sizes fit.
hints: Initialise the vector with round brackets in the initializer list: `m_data(rows * columns, 0.0)` means "this many zeros". With braces it would be a vector of two elements.
